root.claim: A deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Reduce multiplication to digit convolution computed by Fourier transforms, and speed up the two bottlenecks, address rearrangement and butterfly layers, by a recursion with a strict rank saving

motivation.text: Plain transform multiplication spends $\Theta(\log n)$ scans of the data; shaving a power off that factor requires savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving is a fixed power $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ of the logarithm, not a smaller factor such as $\log\log n$, and it refutes the $n\log n$ conjecture.
